authorityPolicy: Primary platform vendors, W3C specifications, WAI/APG, and WCAG guidance only; beta notes are volatility inputs, never silently promoted support floors.
evidencePolicy: External guidance constrains product contracts but never substitutes for source-bound native-browser execution evidence.

rows.sourceFinding: Apple separates Liquid Glass into a functional layer for controls/navigation and advises against using it as the content layer; standard materials remain the content substrate.
rows.localFinding: Current stories use glass broadly enough that semantic role, not class/name or aesthetic preference, must decide every material rung.
rows.transposition: The content field stays warm/legible; functional glass is limited to controls, navigation, and transient chrome. A role/material mismatch is executable RED even when the plate is visually attractive.

rows.sourceFinding: Regular and clear material variants serve different backdrop/legibility conditions, and appearance changes under reduced-transparency and increased-contrast settings.
rows.localFinding: Glass Material advertises adaptive live luminance but reported 0.000/dark over a visibly warm animated field; reduced-transparency and contrast cannot be decorative theme toggles.
rows.transposition: Every glass role declares backdrop complexity, text load, dimming/legibility behavior, reduced transparency, contrast, and failure provenance. Clear material is never a universal default.

rows.authority: W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices — Dialog (Modal) Pattern
rows.sourceFinding: A modal dialog contains its tab sequence, closes on Escape, restores focus appropriately, makes underlying windows inert, and exposes role=dialog plus aria-modal=true and an accessible name.
rows.localFinding: The live Rename workspace dialog focused/restored correctly but had no aria-modal and left #app neither inert nor aria-hidden; body pointer-events:none was the only background barrier.
rows.transposition: Modal and nonmodal scenarios are distinct. Modal acceptance measures focus cycle, Escape owner/restoration, aria-modal/name, and actual background exclusion from accessibility, focus, and hit testing.

rows.authority: W3C WCAG 2.2 — Target Size (Minimum) and Target Size (Enhanced)
rows.sourceFinding: WCAG 2.5.8 uses a 24×24 CSS-pixel minimum with spacing/equivalent/inline/user-agent/essential exceptions; WCAG 2.5.5's 44×44 CSS pixels is enhanced Level AAA guidance.
rows.localFinding: The mobile Dock showed active targets from 20.6 to 40 px high and a source token intended to enforce a 44 px product floor, but unreadable token resolution was masked by fallback.
rows.transposition: The 44 px Dock coarse-target rule is an explicit product floor, not a false statement of WCAG minimum. Gates separately evaluate 24 px conformance/spacing exceptions and the stricter declared product floor on actual hit rectangles.

rows.authority: W3C WCAG 2 working example — Using aria-invalid
rows.sourceFinding: Invalid controls are identified programmatically and their error text is associated through aria-describedby rather than only by a painted border/icon.
rows.localFinding: The live empty-submit witness bridged two fields but left Workspace name native-invalid without aria-invalid; no invalid field had aria-describedby and no error appeared in the accessibility snapshot.
rows.transposition: Each required invalid control exposes one programmatic invalid state and one visible described error, follows a declared focus/announcement policy, and clears the relationship when valid.

rows.sourceFinding: Safari 26.4 moved scroll-driven animations to the compositor; 26.5 fixed dynamic pause, boundary progress, and back-forward-cache restoration defects.
rows.localFinding: Current formation named native scroll timelines but did not explicitly enumerate the newly documented pause/boundary/bfcache failure classes.
rows.transposition: Native support removes the JS shadow writer but does not remove testing: receipts bind exact browser build and exercise dynamic pause/resume, 0/100% boundaries, bfcache back/forward restoration, nested scrollers, resize, and fast drag.

rows.authority: WebKit — News from WWDC26: Safari 27 beta
rows.sourceFinding: Safari 27 beta changes anchor-positioning defaults/keywords and includes focus-scroll and scroll-padding fixes; beta behavior is evidence of volatility, not the stable support floor.
rows.localFinding: The formation used the abstract label Safari-current, which could conceal materially different builds and feature semantics.
rows.transposition: π records exact browser name/version/build and per-feature probes. Stable Safari is the release target; Safari beta is a non-gating forward-compatibility lane unless the product owner explicitly promotes it.

rows.authority: W3C GPU for the Web — WebGPU specification
rows.sourceFinding: WebGPU errors are asynchronous; applications must account for device.lost, uncapturederror, and error scopes, including devices that arrive already lost and resources invalidated by loss.
rows.localFinding: Aurora warned that deferred initialization lacked an error handler, while procedural stories exposed no actual engine identity and current GPU fallback claims could mask internal failure.
rows.transposition: One lifecycle owns error scopes, uncaptured errors, device loss, resource invalidation/recreation policy, terminal failure UI, and teardown. Capability absence may choose a declared peer path; internal failure never silently switches engines.

rows.authority: Chrome for Developers — implementing CSS corner-shape in Blink
rows.sourceFinding: Chrome shipped corner-shape in 2025, including superellipse-based corners; this documents a Blink capability, not cross-engine parity.
rows.localFinding: Glass Material describes corner-shape as Chrome-only progressive enhancement and keeps round border-radius as its floor.
rows.transposition: Superellipse corners may enrich Chrome but cannot carry component identity, geometry, target size, focus, or contrast. Safari/unsupported paths must meet the same semantic product contract without a compatibility alias.

rows.sourceFinding: prefers-reduced-motion requests removal/replacement of nonessential motion; prefers-reduced-transparency requests less transparent/translucent layering; prefers-contrast is a distinct preference.
rows.localFinding: The product combines continuous procedural loops, spring travel, glass transparency, and contrast modes, so one local media query cannot prove cross-system resolution.
rows.transposition: One reactive preference authority projects independently into motion, transparency, and contrast. PRM preserves immediate causal final state with zero nonessential continuous work; reduced transparency preserves hierarchy without glass; contrast remains separately observable.

rows.sourceFinding: Animation timing, effect stacks, composition, replacement, play state, and event ordering are explicit mechanisms; multiple effects can conflict through ordered composition rather than behaving as independent decorations.
rows.localFinding: Prior tranches accumulated overlapping CSS/JS/Dock/procedural writers and accepted source-shape gates that did not prove the actual effect owner.
rows.transposition: Every animated property has one active owner and clock; interruption/reversal/replacement/finish/cancel are semantic states, and gates instrument writer count plus trajectories rather than searching for timing tokens.

rows.authority: W3C CSS View Transitions Levels 1 and 2
rows.sourceFinding: View transitions coordinate old/new visual state through captured transition layers and a lifecycle; Level 2 cross-document behavior is still a Working Draft and conditional on navigation/document state.
rows.localFinding: The demo needs route/focus identity to remain correct whether native view transitions run, are interrupted, are unsupported, or are reduced.
rows.transposition: Native transition support is an enhancement behind a semantic immediate-update floor. Route state, focus, scroll restoration, and final DOM identity are authoritative; captures cannot become stale interaction surfaces.
